author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The University of Rhode Island’s Graduate School of Oceanography will open its Narragansett Bay Campus to the public for Science Saturday on September 26. The free family event runs from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at 215 South Ferry Road and will bring together coastal scientists, engineers, educators and students for tours and hands-on demonstrations.

Dozens of exhibits will cover deep-sea life, Rhode Island’s blue economy, ocean acidification, climate adaptation and underwater sound. Visitors can tour the Ocean Robotics Laboratory and its large test tank, watch live Pacific Ocean exploration through the Inner Space Center, see local marine life at the Ann Gall Durbin Aquarium and examine sediment cores kept in the Marine Geological Samples Laboratory.

Small research boats will be displayed, and guests can try on a survival suit or join volcanic-eruption demonstrations and crafts. URI says the event is certified as a Green Event by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management. Registration is suggested but not required, making the program a broad public showcase for the research facilities and ocean industries concentrated along Narragansett Bay.
dek: The September 26 event at the Narragansett Bay Campus will feature robotics tours, live deep-sea exploration and dozens of hands-on exhibits.
headline: URI opens ocean labs for free Science Saturday
